point_context:
### A Third Voice, the Business Owner: Carrying the Risk

Every week, I check the dashboard for hiring days and costs. When the team fills jobs on time, I can breathe; the business has to keep moving. I see the attraction in reports of much faster hiring at one company and lower costs at another. But if the process appears unfair, public damage, legal costs, and lost trust can come back to me. I decide whether we keep using it.

point_context:
## Why They See It Differently

All three want the right person in the right job. Then the stakes split. The applicant may lose a chance without being fairly seen. The recruiter must keep the process moving and answer for it, but cannot set policy. The owner must keep the business running and carry the result. Their power is unequal: judged, operator, decision-maker. Outside rules narrow the choices too. New York requires a bias audit and notice to applicants; in Europe, hiring AI is high-risk and needs human oversight. No single voice, or simple total, answers the question.
